analysis: Only CHANGELOG.md is visible, as three units: two base excerpts (lines 1404-1993) and one head excerpt (lines 1-220). The base excerpts hold historical release notes and no security-relevant change. The head adds a v0.9.20 candidate section (lines 6-11) raising the default SSD prefix-cache daily write budget from 750 GB to 4 TB, with saved limits and environment overrides unchanged. It also adds unreleased entries: App Attest challenge handling no longer delayed by suspended model/inference work (line 15; the notes say proof, expiry, key-reuse and revocation checks are kept, per TB-011/T-053/T-057), dev/prod build-environment defaults (lines 17-20), and `darkbloom cache set/status` for external encrypted APFS volumes with UUID pinning (lines 22-24; this matches the T-041 mitigation on operator-selected storage). The only finding is the low-severity budget increase tied to T-041, with no source diff to verify. A later pass should check the provider code that sets the default budget (SSDPrefixCachePolicy / the rolling-day ledger) and whether T-041 documents it. It should also check that the App Attest dispatch change in the provider's connection control does not bypass final-dispatch authorization checks; no code was supplied to confirm that.

findings.detail: The changelog says the default SSD prefix-cache rolling-day write budget goes from 750 GB to 4 TB (4,000 decimal GB). This budget is the main control limiting how much a provider's SSD can be written by consumer-triggered cache donations. T-041's endurance guard and the SSD write-endurance entry both rely on it, and it is shared across accounts. A malicious consumer (ADV-002) can submit many unique long prompts over the allowed cache-donation threshold. With the larger default, each provider's SSD absorbs about 5.3x more consumer-induced writes per day before `write_rate_limited` applies. Providers' SSDs are then worn faster, and cached ciphertext and metadata accumulate on the selected volume. T-041 does not state the default budget or record sign-off for the larger value. Only saved limits and environment overrides take precedence, so existing installs without an explicit limit inherit the new default silently. Suggested fix: record the new default and its rationale in T-041, or keep a lower default and let operators opt up through `darkbloom cache set --daily-write-gb`. The changelog shows no implementation diff, so this needs confirmation against the actual policy code.
findings.title: Default SSD cache write budget raised ~5x (750 GB to 4 TB/day) weakens the consumer-driven wear bound; threat model not updated
